correctness.rationale: Exact four Klein-model distance constraints and hyperbolic area element yield full superlevel set. A three-contact triangular blow-up at each of two nonsquare maxima yields \(L^{3/2}/[\pi(2c^2-1)]\); a four-contact square gives \(2/\pi\); the critical \(c^2=1/2+\lambda\sqrt h\) expansion yields a bounded parabolic limiting region, its exact integrated area, the pinch threshold \(2^{-3/4}\), and total-variation conditional shape convergence. Tightness follows from uniqueness of the square maximizer plus the two exact constraints. Nine one-dimensional exact-area quadrature comparisons independently approach the correct coefficients. No finite test substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: A natural observable—rare points whose nearest-side distance nearly achieves the ideal quadrilateral inradius—has a singular shape-dependent coefficient, a genuine \(h^{3/2}\) critical window, and an exact nonanalytic pinch of conditional rare-event geometry. This resolves the nonuniformity of the obvious \(h^2\) fixed-shape limits using a novel second-order anisotropic scaling, and supplies exact coefficients and conditional distributions rather than a routine re-expression of inball center locations.
